Alex — thanks for the clear notes and for looping Maya in. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so everyone has alignment:

Recap:
- Hosted API: multi-tenant shared pool, lowest time-to-value. Best-effort isolation; we do prefix/KV caching and request routing to reduce cross-tenant interference but there is no tenant-boundary SLA for noisy-neighbor performance. Good for early dev and non-SaaS-critical workloads.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for your tenant with predictable throughput and improved isolation. We provide SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for Dedicated contracts and can run isolation tests as part of the PoC.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer-controlled networking and stronger isolation with customer-managed infrastructure — recommended when you need compliance (PCI, specific data residency) and tight audit controls.

Noisy-neighbor mitigation (short):
- Scheduling & pooling: Dedicated uses tenant-dedicated pools (no co-tenant scheduling on the same GPU for the reserved capacity).
- OS-level isolation: cgroups and container boundaries to limit CPU/memory interference; GPU-level partitioning where available (e.g., MIG on supported hardware).
- Runtime safeguards: request prioritization, preemption policies, and autoscaling buffers to keep tail latency down.

Proposed next steps:
1) Share workload sizing: qps, typical token lengths, and peak concurrency (we're happy to provide a short sizing doc).
2) Scope a 2-week Dedicated PoC focused on isolation tests and SLO measurements (we can supply test harness and collection dashboards).
3) Provide a short "security checklist" doc and our SOC2 attestation + KMS integration notes.
4) Quick call next week to finalize PoC scope — I've CC'd Vivek (solutions engineering) who'll run the technical scoping.

Hi Alex / Maya — Vivek here, solutions engineering. Wanted to answer the specific security questions and propose a PoC scope you can take to the team.

1) Dedicated isolation model:
- Dedicated (reserved) capacity gives you an isolated pool. In most configurations we run tenant workloads on dedicated instances (no other customers scheduled on those instances). On supported hardware we can also use GPU partitioning (NVIDIA MIG) but we typically recommend dedicated-instance pools for strict isolation requirements.
- For Dedicated pools we avoid colocating other tenant containers on the same physical host. That provides strong protection against GPU saturation/noisy neighbors.

2) Example noisy-neighbor on Hosted and mitigations:
- Example: a tenant with bursty token generation may cause increased GPU utilization and queuing, which can raise tail latency for other tenants in the same pool. In Hosted we detect this via realtime telemetry (per-tenant token/latency delta) and take actions: rate-limiting the noisy tenant, auto-bursting extra capacity if available, or routing new requests to alternate nodes. Hosted is best-effort: we do not provide an isolation SLA but have many mitigations to reduce impact.

3) Dedicated PoC checklist (2-week):
- Baseline: run synthetic and representative workloads to collect p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput.
- Isolation test: introduce a noisy synthetic workload on a neighboring host and observe tail latency impact on your reserved pool (should be negligible).
- Failure modes: simulate node failures and validate autoscaling/fallback.
- Production traffic replay: replay a subset of real traffic and verify SLO compliance under peak load windows.
- Security checks: validate KMS integration, VPC peering, and audit log delivery to your collector.

SLOs / SLAs:
- We publish performance profiles per model and hardware. For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed availability and can commit to measured latency targets in commercial contracts (targets depend on model size and request profile; we're happy to include explicit p95/p99 targets in the PoC scoping doc).

Next actions:
- I'll share an "isolation & SLOs" matrix and a PoC scoping doc (attached). If that looks good, propose we schedule a 30-minute scoping call with your infra/security team this week.
